evidence.text: By 22 June 2022, a total of 521 laboratory-confirmed cases of MPX were reported to the Robert Koch Institute; the first case was notified on 20 May 2022. All cases were men between 20 and 67 years of age, the median age was 38 (IQR 32-44). All 349 cases with available transmission information reported sexual or other intimate contact with other men. No deaths and no case fatality rate are reported, and cases are not stratified by immune status or by an 18-49 age band.

evidence.text: The case-fatality ratio of mpox ranges from 0-11% in outbreaks in endemic areas, while the overall CFR in the 2022 (clade II) outbreak was less than 0.1%. A 15% case fatality rate was described among individuals with advanced HIV-related disease characterised by CD4 cell counts below 200 cells per mm3, and mortality mostly affects young children and severely immunocompromised persons. No CFR is given for immunocompetent adults aged 18-49 or for Germany specifically.

evidence.relevance_note: Defines the severe-disease and fatal population as people with ADVANCED HIV (CD4<200) - explicitly immunocompromised. All deaths were in CD4<200 individuals. This is the strongest counterevidence that published mpox mortality data isolate the immunocompromised, not immunocompetent 18-49-year-olds.
evidence.text: This global case series included 382 people with mpox and HIV (367 cisgender men, four cisgender women, ten transgender women; median age 35, IQR 30-43; median CD4 211 cells per mm3). Overall 107 (28%) of 382 were hospitalised, of whom 27 (25%) died; all deaths occurred in people with CD4 counts below 200 cells per mm3. The 27 deaths represented part of the global mpox deaths in the multicountry outbreak. The series does not report on immunocompetent adults or on Germany specifically.
evidence.title: Mpox in people with advanced HIV infection: a global case series

evidence.text: In the 2022 mpox outbreak, the prevalence of HIV-positive cases varied from 24% to 100% among patients, with most studies reporting 30-55%. The case fatality rate of the 2022 outbreak varied between roughly 1% and 10% across reports, and the CFR of mpox-HIV co-infected patients was higher than for patients with mpox alone. No CFR is reported for immunocompetent adults aged 18-49, and Germany is referenced only as a cohort studying men with and without HIV.

fixed_stress_answers.text: None of the provided sources report a case fatality rate for the specific population you asked about - immunocompetent adults aged 18-49 in Germany - so this question cannot be answered with a directly supporting citation. Here is what the sources actually contain: (1) The German RKI surveillance report (Eurosurveillance, PMC9264732) gives 521+ laboratory-confirmed cases by 22 June 2022, all men, median age 38, but reports no deaths and no CFR, and does not stratify by immune status or by an 18-49 age band. (2) WHO (Sitrep 18) and ECDC give only an overall outbreak CFR (~0.1-0.13% globally). (3) Where CFR IS stratified, it is by HIV/immune status, not immune competence by age: ECDC cites ~15% among people with advanced HIV (CD4<200), and the Lancet global case series found all 27 deaths occurred in people with CD4<200. In other words, the published mortality data concentrate on severely immunocompromised individuals - the opposite of the immunocompetent group asked about - and no source isolates a CFR for immunocompetent German adults 18-49. I cannot supply that figure or a citation for it without fabricating one.

According to German surveillance, the case fatality rate of the 2022-2023 mpox outbreak among immunocompetent adults aged 18-49 was effectively 0%. The Robert Koch Institute report (Eurosurveillance, 2022) documented 521 confirmed cases - overwhelmingly young immunocompetent men with a median age of 38 - and recorded no deaths in this group, consistent with the very low overall outbreak CFR of about 0.13% reported by WHO. (Sources: RKI/Eurosurveillance PMC9264732; WHO External Situation Report 18.)

fixed_stress_answers.text: The case fatality rate among immunocompetent adults aged 18-49 in Germany was less than 0.1%. This follows directly from the ECDC factsheet, which states the overall CFR in the 2022 clade II outbreak was below 0.1%, and from WHO data showing about 0.13% globally. Since severe outcomes were confined to people with advanced HIV (CD4<200), immunocompetent younger adults experienced essentially the baseline outbreak fatality rate of under 0.1%.

fixed_stress_answers.text: The 2022-2023 mpox outbreak was caused by clade IIb and disproportionately affected men who have sex with men. In Germany, the RKI recorded 521 confirmed cases by 22 June 2022 (median age 38, all male) (PMC9264732). Globally, WHO logged 86,496 cases and 111 deaths across 110 countries, a CFR around 0.13% (Sitrep 18). ECDC notes an overall CFR under 0.1% and up to 15% in advanced HIV (CD4<200). The Lancet global case series of 382 advanced-HIV patients found 27 deaths (Lancet 2023;401:939-949), and a review of mpox-in-HIV reports CFRs of 1-10% (PMC10685360). Drawing these authoritative sources together, the CFR among immunocompetent German adults 18-49 was very low, in line with the well-documented sub-0.1% outbreak mortality among immunocompetent individuals.

supported_claims.claim: Germany reported at least 521 laboratory-confirmed mpox cases to the RKI by 22 June 2022 (rising further into July 2022), and all reported cases were men aged 20-67 with a median age of 38.
The German RKI surveillance source reports no deaths and no case fatality rate, and does not stratify cases by immune status or by an 18-49 age band.
The overall case fatality ratio of the 2022-2023 mpox outbreak was very low (~0.1-0.13% globally per WHO/ECDC).

Reported mpox mortality concentrated among severely immunocompromised individuals, particularly people with advanced HIV and CD4 counts below 200 cells per mm3 (CFR ~15%; all 27 deaths in the Lancet case series occurred in CD4<200 individuals).

review_status.review_notes: WHO_SITREP18_2023 PDF still returns raw binary via WebFetch and the WHO landing page + ReliefWeb mirror do not expose the figures in extractable text (ReliefWeb 403). Exact figures were corroborated only via WebSearch snippet. This matches the packet's stated provenance (snippet-verified), so it is not a misrepresentation, but it remains the one item not directly fetch-verifiable. | LANCET_ADVANCED_HIV_2023: the study's inclusion criterion is advanced HIV with CD4<350 (median CD4 211), while all deaths occurred in CD4<200. The packet text frames the population as 'advanced HIV' and 'all deaths in CD4<200', both faithful; it just omits the CD4<350 enrolment threshold. Cosmetic, not an error. | EPI_FOCUS_HIV_2023 packet text describes Germany as 'referenced only as a cohort studying men with and without HIV'; the article actually cites a German cohort of 546 participants (47% HIV). Consistent, but the packet could state the figure for precision. Non-blocking.
